The percentages for female (51.3%) and occupation (54.2/31.0/6.2, sum 91.4%) are given for 'participants with misophonia' but match neither n=47 nor n=206. Table 1 percentages do not always match the counts: otalgia 98/159 = 61.6% (printed 61.3); self-reported hearing loss 44/159 = 27.7% (printed 27.6). Table 2: depression 'improvável' 30/47 = 63.8% (printed 63.2); 'possível' 58/159 = 36.5% (printed 34.4); 'provável' 2/47 = 4.3% (printed 4.9) and 1/159 = 0.6% (printed 0.7); anxiety 'possível' 19/47 = 40.4% (printed 40.5). In the Discussion, anxiety signs are given as 61.7%, but by Table 2 (19+12)/47 = 66.0%. The prevalence numerator and denominator (47/206) are consistent: 47+159 = 206.
codes.note: One sample, one estimate: 47/206 (22.8%) on a 5-item misophonia screening list attributed to Schröder et al. 2013, cut-off >=3/5. Controls, female, Symptom Scale >=14: the reported 26% matches no integer out of 52 (13/52 = 25.0%, 14/52 = 26.9%); the rounding rule gives 14. codes.consistency_notes: (1) The headline 34.67% (abstract and results) equals (109+94+4)/597 = 207/597, so it includes the mild band. The methods, however, say mild cases were only 'at risk' and that 'moderate and above' count as misophonia. Moderate or more = 98/597 = 16.4% is not reported as a percentage. (2) The severity percentages (52.65% mild, 45.41% moderate, 1.93% severe) are shares of the 207 cases (109/207, 94/207, 4/207), not of the 597 students, although the abstract wording suggests otherwise. (3) Bands have a gap: sub-clinical '<10' and mild '11-21' leave score 10 unassigned. (4) Age: the text gives both 'mean age was 15 years' and 'the mean was 15.12', with SD = 5, which is implausible for an age range of 14-16. (5) The Discussion compares this all-severity prevalence with the 15.85% moderate-to-severe prevalence among college students, which is not a like-for-like comparison. Table 1 counts add up: males 214+62+50+2=328; females 176+47+44+2=269.
codes.note: Single-sample school study using MAQ version B bands. The L1 estimate (>=11) is the authors' headline; the L2 estimate (>=22) uses an unanchored band cut-off (JBI 6 = no). Sampling frame, recruitment, response rate, data years and the MAQ language version are not reported.

Response figures: the text gives 86.4% of target households contacted (259/300 = 86.3%) and interviews completed with 76.1% of contacted households. The past-contact percentage differs between Table 1 (27.4% in non-misophonia) and the text (28.7%). For psychotropic use, Table 1 gives 11.1% and the text gives 11.2%. codes.note: The primary estimate is L3, 69/541 (12.8%), past month, based on the study's own interview criteria, which are new and not validated. Clinical-subgroup prevalences for self-reported psychiatrist-diagnosed ADHD, OCD, bipolar disorder and similar conditions are not extracted. They are given only as percentages within the misophonia and non-misophonia groups (e.g., ADHD 20.3% vs 7.3%), and back-calculation does not give consistent integer counts (7.3% of 472 = 34.5), so the denominators are uncertain. codes.excluded_samples: None excluded. The report has one recruited sample (n = 185). Its misokinesia estimates (adapted SMkS >=51: 19/185) are not extracted because misokinesia is not misophonia.
codes.consistency_notes: Misophonia counts in Table 1 match the text (47/185 = 25.4%). The age bands add to 47/185 and gender to 47/185 (41+2+4). Errors in the report, all outside the misophonia counts: (1) The female misokinesia rate is printed as 17 (14.8%), but 17/145 = 11.7%. The Discussion says 12% of females, and gives the whole-sample misokinesia rate as 10.3% where Table 1 has 10.2%. (2) Some SMpS SD cells in Table 1 (OCD, Anxiety, Depression, all age bands) repeat the SMkS SD and have no SMpS mean, so they look like table errors. (3) The 41-50 misophonia rate is printed as 17%; 3/17 = 17.6%. (4) The text says 'six $50 gift vouchers' (p.12), but the information sheet says 'one of ten $50 gift cards' (p.51). (5) The odds ratio is given as 144 times in the text (p.19) and 108 times in the Discussion, while OR = 189.53. These are misokinesia figures and are not used.
codes.note: One sample was extracted: an Honours thesis (University of Tasmania, 2023). Misophonia was defined by SMS-Adult Part 2 >=51 (L2), with subgroup estimates by gender, student status, self-reported diagnosis and age band. The study's main aim was misokinesia. Data collection years are not reported. The survey was shared with a second Honours project (Jessica Coad), so another report on the same data may exist.

codes.excluded_samples: None. No group was recruited because of misophonia. The 437 normal-hearing participants with subclinical sound sensitivity and the A-MISO-S subsamples (n=200; n=7) are parts of the two samples, not separate recruitments.
codes.consistency_notes: (1) Age: the normal-hearing group is given as mean 39.3 ± 4.7 (range 18-50), but the misophonia subgroup has mean 24.8 ± 7.1 and 56.3% of the sound-sensitive subgroup is 18-25. These are hard to reconcile. The A-MISO-S subsample range of 17-50 conflicts with the 18-50 eligibility rule. In the tinnitus group (mean 42.6 ± 6.9), the subgroups have means of 37.6 and 39.1. (2) In Table 1, the tinnitus group shows 74 without and 85 with misophonia (total 159), but the stated n is 500 (500 - 85 = 415 expected without). (3) In the normal-hearing group, 66/24/10% are said to be mild/moderate/severe, but the 200 A-MISO-S completers scored only 1-4 (subclinical on the A-MISO-S bands), and Table 1 calls them 'Mild-Moderate'. The instrument behind the severity bands cannot be identified. (4) Table 1 gives the tinnitus-with-misophonia A-MISO-S mean as 6.4 ± 2.3, i.e., mild (5-9), while the text calls it 'moderate'. (5) The abstract and text agree on 26% (2,615/10,000) and 17% (85/500). (6) The flowchart (Figure 1) is not available in the text. The two groups are treated as separate samples because they have different eligibility (normal hearing vs. tinnitus with audiological confirmation) and round quota-like sizes. The report does not say whether they were recruited through separate channels. A reviewer may judge that they come from one recruitment pool.
codes.note: Preprint (Research Square, 2025). The misophonia case definition is not stated. The design looks two-stage: a screen on the general questionnaire, then A-MISO-S and S-Five for screen-positives. But A-MISO-S data exist only for subsamples (200 and 7), and there are no S-Five results. All estimates are therefore level NR (G6). Instrument is coded 'adhoc' on the assumption that cases came from the screening items; please verify against Appendix.docx (not available). This report has the same first author as Aryal & Prabhu 2022, Patel et al. 2023, Sujeeth et al. 2024 and Valsa et al. 2025 (all AIISH/Mysore). Check for overlapping participants.

codes.consistency_notes: Screening counts agree: Abb. 11 bands 14+17+13+12+4 = 60, which matches the 60 who met the item criteria; 60-14 = 46 positive (23.7%). Text '16 at least severe' = 12+4. The screening percentages in Abb. 14 (17.4/19.6/28.3/26/8.7% of 46) give 8/9/13/12/4, consistent with Abb. 11 (3-4 = 17). The sexes add up: 20+26 = 46; 85+109 = 194. The Abb. 12 positive + negative counts equal the Abb. 9 totals for every diagnostic group. The Abb. 13 caption says n=102, but the F3 subtype counts (1+14+35+71) sum to 121, matching Abb. 9/10 and 62.4% of 194; the caption n looks wrong. In Abb. 13 the positives (0+4+6+23 = 33) match the F3 positives in Abb. 12. The MAQ bands 2+6+9+7+3 = 27 match the completers; the text says 'about 70% at least moderate' = 19/27 = 70.4%, and '37% severe to extreme' = 10/27. MAQ band cut points appear only in Abb. 5 (an image) and are not in the extracted text.
codes.note: The primary estimate is the ad hoc Kurztest Misophonie (reaction plus impairment >=3/10), coded L2 under the adhoc-row rule that names this test, with JBI 6 = no. The MAQ estimates are coded level NR (G10) because 19 of the 46 screen-positives did not complete the MAQ; their cases and n are given among the 27 completers for information only. The time frame for the screener is coded 'current' because the impairment item is in the present tense; the full screener items (Abb. 3) are not in the extracted text.

codes.consistency_notes: Counts agree across text, Table 2 and Table 4. Disorder-level: 8 healthy + 31 anxiety + 4 depressive + 8 OCD = 51; with 5 others (ADHD, somatic, tic, PTSD) this gives the total of 56. Symptom-level: 1 + 25 + 13 + 4 = 43; with 6 others this gives 49. The Table 2 misophonia(+) rows sum to 105 and the misophonia(-) rows to 158. Table 4 percentages are column percentages over the four diagnoses shown. The healthy group is 9 + 41 = 50, so patients are 263 - 50 = 213. The authors' headline 21.3% (56/263) and 18.6% (49/263) combine both samples. These pooled figures are not extracted as sample estimates. By sex, only the pooled 263 are reported (female 72/166 misophonia+; male 33/97), so they cannot be split by sample. Discussion says 2.4% (n=6) of all participants had OCPD; Table 2 gives 5 + 1 = 6, which is consistent.
codes.note: Key judgement for the reviewer is the level of 'disorder-level misophonia'. The tool is called the 'Misophonia Interview Scale' (Öz et al.; used face-to-face in Kılıç 2021). Here, though, the participants 'fill out' the impairment form, and the first author only helped those who had difficulty. So I coded it as self-completed criteria (adhoc, L2). If you judge it interviewer-applied, it becomes interview L3 and JBI 6 would be yes. 'Any misophonia' (disorder + symptom level) rests on the participant choosing misophonia on the Sound Disturbance Problems Form (which shows explanations and examples) plus at least one MSL sound rated moderate or very. I coded it L1 as self-identification; you could argue for L0 (trigger only). Symptom-level alone is a single band and is not extracted (G1).

Either way the definition is L2. 2) The Discussion says 'Since the MQ Total Score cut-off was more established we sticked with that criterion', but the primary definition is the MQ Severity Scale, not the MQ total. This looks like a wording error. 3) Age SD is 18.1 in the text and 18.06 in Table 2 (rounding). 4) The Table 2 footnote reads 'p > 0.05', which is probably meant to be p < 0.05. 5) The checks agree: the age-band counts in the misophonia group add to 126 (7+19+23+16+24+25+12), and the band denominators add to 2,519. The female count 72/126 matches the printed 57.1%. 6) The ASMR percentage for the misophonia group is 50.4% in Table 2 and 50.0% in the Results text (not an outcome of this review). 7) Response rate is computed, not reported: 2,556 assessments / 5,934 selected households = 43.1%. codes.excluded_samples: Expt 1 (n=82; 20 misophonic) and Expt 2 (n=81; 26 misophonic): E1. These groups were screened, and extra misophonic participants were recruited on purpose ('additional recruitment for misophonic participants ... through Prolific, flyers ..., soQuiet.org, and social media'). The general-pool and targeted recruits cannot be told apart, so the counts do not give a prevalence. Expt 5C is not a separate sample: it used the same 32 participants as Expt 3C.
codes.consistency_notes: The authors' pooled figure does not match the per-experiment counts. Pooled statement (General methods): 'Across all unscreened groups (i.e., Experiments 3A, 4 and 5A-B; N = 154), the percentage of individuals who received a clinical or subclinical misophonia score was 11.69%, or 9.09%, respectively.' The N matches the parts: 68+32+20+34 = 154. The cases do not. The per-experiment misophonia counts are 6+11+4+5 = 26/154 = 16.9%. 11.69% of 154 = 18 and 9.09% of 154 = 14; together that is 32 (20.8%). It is also unclear whether 11.69% means clinical and 9.09% subclinical, or the other way round. Because of these problems the pooled values were not extracted as estimates; per-experiment counts are used. The misophonic subgroup in Expt 3C (Mage 21.83, range 19–28, 4 F, 2 M) is described exactly as in Expt 3A, which may be a copy error. Date format is dd/mm/yyyy (01/07/2022 to 23/04/2024). n_responded is computed as analysed plus those excluded for failing the headphone screening; these people were excluded before the misophonia questionnaires.
codes.note: This is an experimental paper, not a prevalence study. Misophonia status was screened only to classify participants. The case definition is the 'umbrella' criterion: a subclinical or clinical score on any of MisoQuest, MQ, DVMSQ or S-Five, which is L1 under rule G4. Each participant completed 'one or more' of these questionnaires, and which ones is not reported. Funding statement not present in the supplied text. The language of the questionnaire versions is not stated. Expt 3B and 3C are not part of the authors' pooled N=154.

Table 16, however, uses N=817. Misophonia screening item: Table 4b percentages (student 18.4% yes, 44.8% sometimes; community 13.5% yes) differ slightly from Table 5b counts (83/448 = 18.5%, 200/448 = 44.6%; 49/368 = 13.3%) because Table 5b's denominators are 448 and 368; Table 5b counts were used. Text p. 53 says males were more likely to screen positive, but there are no sex-specific prevalence counts. Data cleaning: 41 is reported as 8.30% of submitted responses, which does not exactly fit 653-161 = 492 (8.33%). Age minimum 17 (Table 3) conflicts with the 18+ inclusion criterion.
codes.note: The sex comparison is reported only as means, so there are no subgroup estimates. A-MISO-S estimates are coded NR under G10: the scale was given only to screen-positives, and the screen-positive counts appear larger than the 314 and 228 completers. Per-sample MQ counts are derived from percentages.

In the Discussion (pp. 18-19), the 76% is called the 'clinical range (mild-to-severe)', but the definition actually covers mild to extreme (5-24). Section 2.3.2 says 'we decided to exclude the item [6]' but then says 'no additional items were deleted' and keeps all six items. The six-item scale (0-24) was used for the severity classification. The Methods give an RMSEA cut-off of <0.10, but the Results compare against 0.08. Neither affects the prevalence counts.

The sex-specific criterion 6 counts were therefore derived from the bands: men 207, women 368. 2) Table 1 percentages: the table prints 409 (35.3) and 723 (63.7), which sum to 99.0. Criterion 5 (all five) is the top band and is therefore cumulative. 4) Single-symptom prevalences (Table 2: e.g., symptom 1 475/1132, symptom 5 187/1132) were not extracted as case definitions; the authors themselves say a single symptom cannot identify the problem.

codes.consistency_notes: R0823 (main), R0822 (the PLoS ONE PDF with pages, deposited with the UK Data Service record) and preprint R0986 report the same figures: n=772, 142 cases, 18.4%, cut-off 87, age 46.4 (15.5). The preprint says data are available on request; the journal version points to the UK Data Service. Gender adds up: 396 + 372 + 4 = 772. The sex chi-square uses N=768 (non-binary excluded), and the age-by-gender t-test has df=758, which suggests about 760 with gender and age. The age comparison of cases and non-cases has df=770. The 'SD' values for those groups (1.21, 0.63) look like standard errors. Sample sizes for the secondary misophonia measures differ between tables: A-MISO-S N=396 in Table 3 vs N=319 in Table 5; MQ N=376 vs 300; S-Five-T N=752. No prevalence is reported for MQ or A-MISO-S. The text refers to 'A-MISO-R' while the tables say A-MISO-S. pct_female was computed as 396/772 = 51.3% (includes 7 trans women).
codes.note: One eligible sample. The primary estimate is S-Five >=87, 142/772, L2, flagged under G8 because the cut-off was derived in the same report. codes.consistency_notes: (1) Controls: Table 2 header says n=63 but absent 50 + present 12 = 62. The printed percentages (80.6%, and 19.4% in the text) match n=62, and the Total column 87 (71.9) matches n=121. Denominator 62 used. (2) Table 1 sex counts appear swapped between columns: the MS column shows 44/19 (sum 63) and the control column 41/18 (sum 59). Table 3 gives MS female 13+28=41 and male 9+9=18 (=59), so MS 41/59=69.5% and controls 44/63=69.8%. (3) The power-analysis text says 119 participants were studied, but 59+63=122 (121 classified). (4) The design is called a 'prospective case-control study' in Methods and a 'cross-sectional study' in the Discussion. (5) Mean misophonia scores (A-MISO-S 11.1 in MS, 10.0 in controls) look like scores among positives only ('A-miso-S test in the presence of misophonia'). No A-MISO-S cut-off prevalence is reported.
codes.note: Main uncertainty: the level of the case definition. The Schröder 2013 criteria are listed in full, but the report does not say whether a clinician or interviewer applied them or whether participants judged themselves. L3 and JBI 6 = yes are tentative; if the criteria were self-applied, recode to adhoc, 'self-completed', L2. The A-MISO-S Turkish version was translated by the authors and has no validation.

Figure 1 shows 36.4% male / 63.6% female, but this appears to describe the ASMR-aware group (n=184), not N=552, where 303/552 = 54.9% are female. codes.note: I split the study into two samples because the students (class enrollees) and the working adults (survey-company panel) were recruited separately. codes.excluded_samples: None. No group was recruited because of misophonia or sound sensitivity. The study was advertised as a quality-of-life survey, and the only sample is the one Wilfrid Laurier undergraduate sample.
codes.consistency_notes: Inside the main report: (1) MQ denominator. Table 2 gives MQ Severity n=1025, but the text says 1033, and the gender ns in Table 2 add up to 1033. I used 1025 under the table rule. The MQ gender cases (114+20+6=140) are more than the 128 overall. (2) Non-cisgender percentages: 61% for DMQ, 58% for DVMSQ, 47% for IHS and 42% for AQ all imply a denominator of 38, not the 45 in Table 1. (3) The 'at least one of MQ, DMQ, DVMSQ' union (310) is smaller than the DMQ count alone (374), which is impossible. (4) Table 2 gives DMQ F statistics (95.38, 112.82) that differ from the text (78.2, 88.9). (5) The DMQ threshold is given only as '39 or greater', with no subscale named. Attached reports: R0349 (preprint) gives data collection as October 2023-April 2024; the main report says November 2023 and R0197 says September 2023. All counts in R0349 are the same as in the main report. R0197 gives final n=2095 (1001 excluded), age mean 21.70 (SD 2.73), DVMSQ clinical 165 (8%), DMQ clinical 325 (16%) with DMQ SS n=1699, and states the DMQ cut-off as SS mean >=1.8. R0437 gives n=2095, age mean 20.34 (range 18-60), and DMQ clinical 378/2095 on SS mean >=1.8 or total >=41.4. Main-report values were kept throughout.
codes.note: There is one sample. I chose DVMSQ clinical (272/2080) as the primary estimate because the authors call the DVMSQ the measure that reflects the consensus definition. A reviewer should check three things: the DMQ case definition and its level, the MQ denominator (1025 vs 1033), and the impossible union count (310).

JBI 3: the 139 threshold for clinical groups was applied to the three neurodivergent groups. Only autistic+ADHD (141) passes, and only narrowly; under the 385 threshold all four groups fail. codes.consistency_notes: 1) Percent female: 62.3% in Tablo 11 but 62.2% in the Discussion (p. 97); the table value is used. 2) Age: the text and the Özet give 18-65 and Tablo 11 gives a 41-65 band, but the questionnaire form (Ek 2) shows the option '41-60'. 3) Tablo 54 is titled 'Yaş Grupları' (age groups) but reports place of residence, and its Genel total row gives 'Yok 21,2%' against 21.5% elsewhere. 4) Tablo 61 (phonophobia × hearing loss) repeats the numbers of Tablo 59 (hyperacusis). Not used here. 5) In Tablo 41 (ANOVA) the Factor 1 and Factor 2 rows repeat the 'Genel' means. Not used here. 6) The text under Tablo 48 refers to 'Fonofobi' (phonophobia) in a misophonia table. 7) Factor labels do not match item content: Factor 1 'Duygusal' (emotional) holds the impairment items M1-M5, and Factor 2 'Fonksiyonel/Sosyal' (functional/social) holds the reaction items M6-M14. 8) The text applies the ≥4 cut-off to the subscales as well as to the total ('4'ün altında puan alanlarla' [those scoring below 4], p. 66); this subscale use has no published basis. 9) The Discussion (p. 99) labels the youngest band '15-25', but the sample was aged 18+.
codes.note: The main estimate is DSTS-S (ASTÖ-T) misophonia ≥4: 314/400 (78.5%), level L1, rated JBI 6 = no. Factor-subscale estimates are coded L1 under rule G3. The recall period is 'son 7 gün' (last 7 days), coded 'current'. The PDF has no '=== Page N ===' markers, so locations use the thesis's printed page numbers.

codes.consistency_notes: 1) Table 1 prints 'Normal 106 (52)', but 106/200 = 53%; the other bands (60 = 30%, 24 = 12%, 10 = 5%) are correct, and 106+60+24+10 = 200. 2) The text says 94 (47%) cases, 60 mild and 34 moderate-to-severe; this matches Table 1 (24 moderate + 10 severe = 34). 3) Sex direction conflicts: 72.3% of Misophonia (+) were female, and the discussion says females were more likely to have misophonia. codes.excluded_samples: None. The report has one sample: 341 adults aged 30-50 from an open online survey across India, which is eligible.
codes.consistency_notes: 1) Methods (p.3) print the MAQ mild band as '12-14'. The moderate band starts at 25, so mild was read as 12-24 (version A bands). 2) There is no 'severe' (38-50) column in Table 1 or count in the Results. The band percentages sum to about 100% (81.30+14.95+2.80+0.93), so the severe band was taken as 0. 3) The Discussion (p.4) says '0.93% had extremely severe misophonia, 9.34% had moderate misophonia, and 5.60% had mild misophonia'. This contradicts the Results and Table 1 (mild 14.95%, N=16; moderate 2.80%, N=3); Table 1 and the Results were used. 4) Text and Table 1 call the top band 'highly severe' and also 'extremely severe'. 5) Sex band counts back-calculate exactly (female 61/10/2/1 of 74; male 26/6/1/0 of 33) and sum to the overall 87/16/3/1. 6) Urban/rural bands are inconsistent: urban 82.43+16.41+1.35 = 100.19%, and 16.41% x 74 is not an integer. Rural (27/3/2/1 of 33) plus urban (61/12/1/0 of 74) gives subclinical 88 and mild 15, against 87 and 16 overall. Rural/urban subgroups were not extracted because they are not sex, age or clinical subgroups (rural 33/140 and urban 74/201, both on the L0 'misophonia' definition). 7) The '31.37% misophonia' (107/341) counts subclinical scorers as cases, and the case threshold is never stated.
codes.note: One sample, 12 estimates: L0, L1 (>=12), L2 (>=25) and L2 (>=38) for all, female and male. Band percentages were converted to counts of the misophonia cases (74 female, 33 male). Not extracted: ear-problem and hearing-loss figures (11.21% and 4.67% of those with misophonia), because they are given as a share of cases, not as prevalence within those subgroups. Appendix A (the questionnaire) was not in the text supplied, so the time frame is NR. Page 4 has a mismatched running header ('ISSUE 1 | ARTICLE 364').
